Where it began

Shreyas Iyer was born in Chembur, in what was then Bombay, on 6 December 1994. At 18 he was spotted at the Shivaji Park Gymkhana by the coach Pravin Amre, who shaped his early cricket.

In the age-group sides, his teammates liked to compare him to Virender Sehwag, which tells you something about how he went about it. He went on to play for Mumbai, and in the 2015–16 Ranji Trophy he made 1,321 runs, more than anyone else that season.

The player

Iyer's first taste of Test cricket came before he had even played one. Called up as a stand-in in 2017, he came on as a substitute fielder against Australia and ran out Steve O'Keefe.

His actual debut, against New Zealand in November 2021, was quite something. He received his cap from Sunil Gavaskar, made a hundred in the first innings and a fifty in the second, the first Indian to manage both on debut. By October 2026 he had played 14 Tests, making 811 runs at 36.86 with five fifties to go with that debut hundred, and he won a match award for two fifties on a turning pitch against Sri Lanka in 2022.

What made him special

At his best Iyer is a joy to watch, and he can score in a hurry: he once took 31 runs from a single over in an ODI. He has a gift for big occasions, too. He made a century against New Zealand in the 2023 World Cup semi-final, and he was in the India sides that lifted the Asia Cup in 2023 and the Champions Trophy two years later. He has twice been named the ICC's player of the month.

His Test bowling is a gentler story. He has turned his arm over in Tests without yet taking a wicket, which only means the first one, when it comes, will be enjoyed all the more.

Away from the middle

Iyer is a natural captain. He has led Mumbai, and in the Indian Premier League he took Kolkata Knight Riders to the title in 2024. No other captain has led three different IPL teams into a final.

In June 2026 he became India's T20I captain, and in October he led India to the gold medal at the Asian Games. A few days later he made his first T20I hundred, an unbeaten 102 against the West Indies. He speaks Tamil, Marathi and Hindi, which can only help in a dressing room drawn from all over India.

And finally

Most players spend years hoping to make an impression on a Test match. Iyer made his before his debut, from the outfield, holding nothing more than the ball he was about to throw.
